methods.name: session.close_layer
methods.description: Close a floating layer and every block in it.

layer_id.description: The floating layer to close. Every block in it closes too.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: `layer_id` must name a floating layer. Naming the window's layout, the layer of kind `tiled` in `session.view`, fails the call with `bad_request`. Close the window with `session.close_window` instead.
The server closes every block in the layer, which ends the programs running in them. The call returns once the blocks have closed.
If the layer had focus, focus returns to the layer that had it before, at the block last focused there. Otherwise focus doesn't change.
If the layer held the window's last blocks, the server closes the window too.
If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `layer_id` names no layer in the session, it fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.close_window
methods.description: Close a window and every block in it.

window_id.description: The window to close. Leave it out to close the active window. Every block in it closes too.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: The server closes every block in the window, which ends the programs running in them. The call returns once the blocks have closed.
If the window was active, the window after it becomes active, or the one before it if it was last.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `window_id` names a window that isn't in the session, it fails with `not_found`. A window leaves the session as soon as a close starts, so closing the same window twice also fails with `not_found`.
If `window_id` is left out and the session has no windows, the call fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.create
methods.description: Create a session, optionally with its first windows already in it.

label.description: The session's label, up to 128 characters. Leave it out to let the server choose one, such as quiet-meadow.

window_label.description: The window's label, up to 128 characters. Leave it out for a label made from the window's ID, such as Window 89abcdef.

layout.description: The blocks to create in the window and how to arrange them. Required. Each node holds either block, with a flavor and optional options and label, or split, with direction, before, after, and an optional ratio.

initial_windows.description: Windows to create with the session, in order. The last one becomes the active window. If any of them fails, the server creates no session.

block_ids.description: The new blocks' IDs, in layout order: each split's before side comes ahead of its after side.

revision.description: The session's revision after the window was created.

initial_windows.description: The windows created with the session, in the order requested.

validation_notes: Every argument is optional. With none, the server creates a session with no windows.
If `label` is left out or empty, the server picks one that no other session has, such as `quiet-meadow`.

The server sends `session_created` only once every window in `initial_windows` is ready, so no client sees a half-built session. If any window fails, the server closes the session and its blocks, and the call fails.
The calling client becomes the owner of every block in the initial windows.
The call doesn't attach the connection to the new session. Call `session.attach` to receive its events.
If a layout is malformed, the call fails with `bad_request` before any block is created. A flavor that no creator provides fails with `not_found`.
If the server already has as many sessions as it allows, the call fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.describe_block
methods.description: Get a block's details and the methods, events, and actions it provides.

block_id.description: The block to describe. It may be a detached block.
The block's ID.

creator_name.description: The creator that made the block, such as com.superlogical.terminal.

flavor.description: The flavor the block was made from, such as com.superlogical.terminal.shell.

host_id.description: Identifies the machine and account the block runs as. If it equals your local server's host_id, the block sees the same files you do. Otherwise treat the block as remote.

placement.description: Whether the block is in a window: 'placed' or 'detached'. Treat a value you don't know as 'detached'.

window_id.description: The window the block is in. Left out when the block is detached.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

block.description: The block, described as in session.list_blocks.

events.description: The block events, by name. Each value is a JSON Schema for the event's fields.

methods.description: The block methods, by short name.

input_schema.description: A JSON Schema for the method's arguments.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema for the method's result.

name.description: The action's short name, such as reset. Its full name, used in key bindings, is the creator's name, a dot, and this name.

title.description: The name to show a person, such as Reset Terminal.

description.description: A sentence about what the action does, to show under its title in a menu or command palette.

category.description: A group of related actions, such as Pane.

keywords.description: More words to search for the action by, separated by spaces.

args.description: The fixed arguments the method is called with when the action runs. Left out when there are none.

repeats.description: True if holding the key down should run the action again, as holding an arrow key does.

actions.description: The actions that call this method, in the order the creator declares them.

api.description: The methods and events the block provides.

validation_notes: `api` lists the methods and events the block provides, in the same form as `block_creator.list`. Call a method as `<creator>.<method>` with `session_id`, `block_id`, and its arguments under `args`.
If `block_id` names a block that isn't in the session, or one that is closing, the call fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.destroy
methods.description: Destroy a session and close every block in it.

session_id.description: The session to destroy. Every block in it closes.

validation_notes: The server closes every window and block in the session. Closing a terminal hangs up the program running in it, as closing a terminal window does.
The call returns once the session has closed. `session_destroyed` is the last event about the session, though a `client_script_events_dropped` event for it can still follow.
The connection must be attached to the session, with `session.attach`, `session.bootstrap`, or `session.attach_all`, or the call fails with `conflict`.
If `session_id` names no session, the call fails with `session_not_found`.

methods.name: session.detach
methods.description: Detach the connection from a session. The connection stays open and the session keeps running.
validation_notes: The connection's other attachments, and any events it receives through `session.attach_all`, continue as before.
The client leaves the session. The server sends `client_disconnected`, and each block the client owned passes to the next client in line for it, if there is one.
If the connection isn't attached to the session, the call succeeds and changes nothing, even if the session doesn't exist.
A `session.attach` for the same session that is still in progress isn't canceled. This call succeeds without detaching, and the attach completes.
If the connection attaches to the session again later, its client keeps the same `client_id`.

methods.name: session.detach_block
methods.description: Take a block out of its window without closing it. The block keeps running.

block_id.description: The block to detach. It keeps running but leaves its window.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: `session.list_blocks` lists the block with `placement` set to `detached`, and `session.move_block` places it in a window again.
Detaching a block that is already detached succeeds and changes nothing.
If the block was the last one in its window, the window closes too. If it was the only block in a floating layer, the layer closes.
If the block had focus, another block in its window gets focus.
To close the block instead, call `block.close`.
If `block_id` names a block that isn't in the session, the call fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.disown_block
methods.description: Give up the calling client's claim on blocks. The result lists each block's owner.

block_ids.description: The blocks to give up. Leave it out or empty to give up every block in the session.

block_id.description: The block's ID.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: Each block and its owner after this call.

validation_notes: The calling client must be attached to the session, with `session.attach` or `session.bootstrap`. A connection that only called `session.attach_all` fails with `bad_request`.
A block the caller owned passes to the next connected client in line for it, or is left with no owner. For a block the caller doesn't own, the caller only leaves the line.
`blocks` lists each block's owner after the call, in the order of `block_ids`, with a repeated ID listed once. When you give up every block, they are sorted by `block_id`.
Every change of owner sends `block_owner_changed`. If a block in a window changes owner, the call also sends one `session_view_changed`.
If any ID in `block_ids` isn't a block in the session, the call fails with `bad_request` and changes nothing.

methods.name: session.float_block
methods.description: Move a block out of its window's layout into a new floating layer.

block_id.description: The block to float. It must be in its window's layout, not already in a floating layer.

bounds.description: Where the new floating layer sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height. It must fit inside the window.

anyOf.description: A rectangle as [x, y, w, h]. x and y place its top-left corner and w and h give its size, each as a fraction of the window's width or height.

x.description: The left edge, as a fraction of the window's width.

y.description: The top edge, as a fraction of the window's height.

w.description: The width, as a fraction of the window's width.

h.description: The height, as a fraction of the window's height.

anyOf.description: The same rectangle as an object, the form that earlier clients send.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call.

validation_notes: `bounds` is measured from the window's top-left corner. Its width and height must be greater than 0.
The new layer is in the block's own window, in front of every other floating layer there.
Focus and the active window don't change. If the window was zoomed, the zoom ends.
Floating the last block of a window's layout leaves the layout empty. The window stays open, and its layer of kind `tiled` in `session.view` keeps the same `layer_id`.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `block_id` names a block that isn't in any window, including a detached block, it fails with `not_found`, and bad `bounds` fail with `bad_request`.
If the block is already in a floating layer, the call fails with `bad_request`.

methods.name: session.focus_block
methods.description: Focus a block, and make its window the active window if it isn't.

block_id.description: The block to focus. It must be in a window, which becomes the active window.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: The block can be in the window's layout or in a floating layer. If it isn't already its window's focused block, any zoom in that window ends.

methods.name: session.focus_direction
methods.description: Move focus to the nearest block to the left, right, above, or below.

direction.description: Which way to move focus from the focused block in the active window.

wrap.description: Whether to continue from the opposite edge when no block lies that way. Defaults to false. Older servers ignore it and always wrap.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If the session has no windows, it fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.help

methods.name: session.list
methods.description: List the sessions on the server.

sessions.description: Every session on the server. New sessions go at the end, and session.move changes the order.

validation_notes: Sessions are listed in the order they were created, until `session.move` changes that order. `session.attach_all` and `session.bootstrap` list them in the same order.

methods.name: session.list_blocks
methods.description: List every block in the session, including detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block's ID.

creator_name.description: The creator that made the block, such as com.superlogical.terminal.

flavor.description: The flavor the block was made from, such as com.superlogical.terminal.shell.

host_id.description: Identifies the machine and account the block runs as. If it equals your local server's host_id, the block sees the same files you do. Otherwise treat the block as remote.

placement.description: Whether the block is in a window: 'placed' or 'detached'. Treat a value you don't know as 'detached'.

window_id.description: The window the block is in. Left out when the block is detached.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: Every block in the session, including detached blocks.

validation_notes: Treat a `placement` you don't recognize like `detached`. The block exists and you can call its methods, but don't assume where it is shown.
Blocks are sorted by `block_id`.
To see where each block sits in its window and which one has focus, call `session.view`.

methods.name: session.list_clients
methods.description: List the clients attached to the session.

kind.description: How the server identified the client: 'peer' (Unix socket credentials), 'windows_peer' (named pipe credentials), 'tailscale' (a Tailscale login), or 'anonymous' (not identified). Show a kind you don't know by its name.

transport.description: How the client first reached Rex: 'unix', 'named_pipe', 'tcp', or 'tailscale'. A login server passes it on unchanged.

display.description: A readable name for the client, such as uid 501 or alice@example.com. It can be out of date or shared, so compare uid, sid, or user_id instead.

remote_addr.description: The client's network address. Left out when there is none, such as on a Unix socket.

uid.description: The client's Unix user ID. Only for kind peer.

gid.description: The client's Unix group ID. Only for kind peer.

pid.description: The client's process ID when it connected, for kind peer or windows_peer, if known. Process IDs are reused, so use it only for debugging.

sid.description: The client's Windows security identifier, which survives account renames. Only for kind windows_peer.

user_id.description: The Tailscale user ID that owns the client's device. Only for kind tailscale. Check tags before treating it as a person.

login_name.description: The client's Tailscale login name, usually an email address. For display only.

node.description: The name of the client's Tailscale device. Only for kind tailscale.

tags.description: The Tailscale tags of the client's device. Any tag means the client is a machine, such as a CI runner, not a person.

path.description: The route the client took to this server, for troubleshooting. Entries include 'tailscale' (built-in Tailscale), 'tailnet' and 'tailnet-serve' (the machine's own Tailscale), and 'login-server' (passed on by a login server).

principal.description: Who the client is, as the server identified it when it accepted the connection.

kind.description: What sort of program the client is: app, cli, agent, or other. Left out if the client didn't say. Treat a kind you don't know as other.

platform.description: What the client runs on: macos, ios, linux, windows, freebsd, web, or other. Left out if the client didn't say. Treat a platform you don't know as other.

name.description: The program's name, such as Rex.app or rex.

version.description: The program's version, as the program prints it, such as 1.6.0.

label.description: The client's label, such as studio. Two clients can share a label.

info.description: What the client says about itself, such as its name and version, for showing to people. Left out if it said nothing.

connected_at.description: When the client attached to this session, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

connection_state.description: Whether the client has a connection: connected, or lost if it dropped and the client may still reconnect. Treat a missing or unknown value as connected.

connection_lost_at.description: When the server noticed the connection drop, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Set only while connection_state is lost. A client that doesn't reconnect within 60 seconds leaves the session.

clients.description: The clients attached to the session, in the order they attached.

validation_notes: Only clients attached with `session.attach` or `session.bootstrap` are listed. A connection that only called `session.attach_all` isn't. To list every connected client, call `client.list`.

methods.name: session.lower_layer
methods.description: Move a floating layer to the back, or just below another floating layer.

layer_id.description: The floating layer to move back.

relative_layer_id.description: Another floating layer in the same window to place it just below. Leave it out to move it behind every other floating layer.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: `layer_id` must name a floating layer. Naming the window's layout, the layer of kind `tiled` in `session.view`, fails the call with `bad_request`.
A floating layer never goes behind the window's layout. At the back, it sits behind every other floating layer and in front of the layout.
If the layer is already in place, the call changes nothing. Focus and the layer's bounds never change.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `layer_id` names no layer in the session, it fails with `not_found`, and if `relative_layer_id` is the same as `layer_id`, it fails with `bad_request`.
If `relative_layer_id` names a layer of kind `tiled`, or a layer in another window, the call fails with `bad_request`. If it names no layer in the session, it fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.move
methods.description: Move a session to another place in the order that session.list returns.

before_session_id.description: The session to place it just before. Leave it out to move the session to the end.

validation_notes: The order is the same for every client. Each move that changes it sends `session_moved` with the same `session_id` and `before_session_id`.
Moving a session to where it already is succeeds and changes nothing.
The connection must be attached to the session it moves, with `session.attach`, `session.bootstrap`, or `session.attach_all`, or the call fails with `conflict`.
If `before_session_id` names the session being moved, the call fails with `bad_request`.
If either ID names no session, the call fails with `session_not_found`, and the message says which one.

methods.name: session.move_block
methods.description: Move a block, or place a detached one, in a new split beside another block.

block_id.description: The block to move. It may be detached or placed in any window.

anchor_block_id.description: The block to place it beside. It must be placed in a window.

direction.description: How to divide the anchor's space: 'horizontal' for side by side or 'vertical' for one above the other. Defaults to horizontal.

side.description: Where the moved block goes: 'before' for the left or top part, or 'after' for the right or bottom part. Defaults to after.

ratio.description: The fraction of the space that the before part gets, greater than 0 and less than 1. Defaults to 0.5.

created_split_id.description: The split created beside the anchor.

removed_split_id.description: The split that held the block before the move, which the move removed. Left out if no split was removed, such as for a detached block.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call.

validation_notes: The block and the anchor can be in different windows or layers.
If the block had focus in its window, focus moves with it and its new window becomes active. A detached block doesn't take focus.
Zoom ends in every window the move changes.

If the move empties a floating layer, the server removes it. If it empties a whole window, the server closes the window. A window's layout that empties while the window still has floating layers stays, with the same `layer_id`.
Apart from the two splits named in the result, every split keeps its ID.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `block_id` and `anchor_block_id` are the same, or `ratio` is out of range, it fails with `bad_request`. If either block isn't in the session, or the anchor isn't in a window, it fails with `not_found`.
If the block is detached or in another window, and the anchor's window already has as many blocks as it allows, the call fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.move_window
methods.description: Move a window to another place in the session's window order.

before_window_id.description: The window to place it just before. Leave it out to move the window to the end.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: The window order is the order of `windows` in `session.view` and of the tabs in Rex.app. `session.focus_next_window` and `session.focus_previous_window` follow it.
The active window, focus, and the windows' blocks don't change. If the window is already in place, the call changes nothing.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If either window isn't in the session, it fails with `not_found`, and if `before_window_id` is the same as `window_id`, it fails with `bad_request`.

methods.name: session.new_block
methods.description: Create a block without placing it in a window. Place it later with session.move_block.

flavor.description: The flavor of block to create, such as com.superlogical.terminal.shell. block_creator.list lists them.

options.description: Settings for the block's creator, in the shape of the flavor's options_schema from block_creator.list.

label.description: The block's label, up to 128 characters. Defaults to the flavor's short name, such as shell.

block_id.description: The new block's ID. The block is detached until you place it with session.move_block.

revision.description: The session's revision. Creating a detached block doesn't change it.

validation_notes: The server passes `options` to the flavor's creator unchanged.
The block starts detached: it runs, sends events, and answers method calls, but no window shows it. `session.move_block` can place it beside a block that is in a window.
The calling client becomes the block's owner.
A malformed `flavor` or `label` fails with `bad_request`. A flavor that no creator provides fails with `not_found`.
If the server already has as many blocks as it allows, the call fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.new_layer
methods.description: Create blocks in a new floating layer at the front of a window.

window_id.description: The window to add the floating layer to. Leave it out to use the active window.

bounds.description: Where the new floating layer sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height. It must fit inside the window.

anyOf.description: A rectangle as [x, y, w, h]. x and y place its top-left corner and w and h give its size, each as a fraction of the window's width or height.

x.description: The left edge, as a fraction of the window's width.

y.description: The top edge, as a fraction of the window's height.

w.description: The width, as a fraction of the window's width.

h.description: The height, as a fraction of the window's height.

anyOf.description: The same rectangle as an object, the form that earlier clients send.

layout.description: The blocks to create in the floating layer and how to arrange them. Each node holds either block, with a flavor and optional options and label, or split, with direction, before, after, and an optional ratio.

focus.description: Whether to make the window active and focus the first new block. Defaults to false.

block_ids.description: The new blocks' IDs, in layout order: each split's before side comes ahead of its after side.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call.

validation_notes: `bounds` is measured from the window's top-left corner. Its width and height must be greater than 0.

A `block` node in `layout` starts one new block from a `flavor`, such as `com.superlogical.terminal.shell`. A `split` node divides its space in two and holds another node in each of `before` and `after`.

In a `split` node, `direction` is `horizontal` to put `before` on the left of `after`, or `vertical` to put it on top. `ratio` is the fraction of the space that `before` gets, greater than 0 and less than 1. It defaults to 0.5.
`layout` always starts new blocks. To move a block that is already in a window's layout into a floating layer, use `session.float_block`.
The new layer starts in front of every other floating layer in the window.
Either the whole layout is created or none of it is. If a block fails to start, the server closes the blocks it already started, and the call fails.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `window_id` names a window that isn't in the session, or no creator provides a `flavor`, it fails with `not_found`. Bad `bounds`, or a malformed `layout` or `flavor`, fail with `bad_request`.
If `window_id` is left out and the session has no windows, the call fails with `conflict`.
If the call would go past a limit on blocks per window or blocks on the server, it fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.new_split
methods.description: Create blocks in a new split beside an existing block or split.

anchor_id.description: The block or split whose space to split. A block ID splits that one block. A split ID puts the new blocks beside that split and everything under it. Leave it out to split the focused block of window_id, or of the active window. Don't send it with window_id.

window_id.description: The window whose focused block to split. Send it only when anchor_id is left out.

direction.description: How to divide the anchor's space: 'horizontal' for side by side or 'vertical' for one above the other.

side.description: Where the new blocks go: 'before' for the left or top part, or 'after' for the right or bottom part.

ratio.description: The fraction of the space that the before part gets, greater than 0 and less than 1. Defaults to 0.5.

layout.description: The blocks to create beside the anchor and how to arrange them. Each node holds either block, with a flavor and optional options and label, or split, with direction, before, after, and an optional ratio.

focus.description: Whether to make the anchor's window active and focus the first new block. Defaults to false.

anchor_id.description: The block or split whose space was split. If the request didn't name one, this is the focused block the server used.

block_ids.description: The new blocks' IDs, in layout order: each split's before side comes ahead of its after side.

split_ids.description: The IDs of the splits this call created: first the one at the anchor, then the new layout's own splits in layout order.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call.

validation_notes: The server picks the block to split before it starts the new blocks, so a focus change while they start doesn't move the split.

A `block` node in `layout` starts one new block from a `flavor`, such as `com.superlogical.terminal.shell`. A `split` node divides its space in two and holds another node in each of `before` and `after`.

In a `split` node, `direction` is `horizontal` to put `before` on the left of `after`, or `vertical` to put it on top. `ratio` is the fraction of the space that `before` gets, greater than 0 and less than 1. It defaults to 0.5.
Any zoom in the window ends, whether or not `focus` is set.

If `anchor_id` is a split ID, the new split takes that split's place. The old split, with everything under it, goes on one side and `layout` on the other. Anchoring a layer's top split makes the new blocks span the whole layer. A layer with one block has no split, so anchor its block instead.
Splits that already existed keep their IDs.
Either the whole layout is created or none of it is. If a block fails to start, the server closes the blocks it already started, and the call fails.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `window_id` names a window that isn't in the session, or no creator provides a `flavor`, it fails with `not_found`. Sending both `anchor_id` and `window_id`, a bad `ratio`, or a malformed `layout` or `flavor` fail with `bad_request`.

If `anchor_id` names a block that isn't in a window, including a detached block, or a split that isn't in any window, the call fails with `not_found`. If both `anchor_id` and `window_id` are left out and the session has no windows, it fails with `conflict`.
If the call would go past a limit on blocks per window or blocks on the server, it fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.new_window
methods.description: Create a window and the blocks in its layout. It becomes the active window by default.

window_label.description: The window's label, up to 128 characters. Leave it out for a label made from the window's ID, such as Window 89abcdef.

layout.description: The blocks to create in the window and how to arrange them. Required. Each node holds either block, with a flavor and optional options and label, or split, with direction, before, after, and an optional ratio.

focus.description: Whether to make the new window the active window. Defaults to true. A session with no active window always makes the new one active.

block_ids.description: The new blocks' IDs, in layout order: each split's before side comes ahead of its after side.

revision.description: The session's revision after the window was created.

validation_notes: A `block` node in `layout` starts one new block from a `flavor`, such as `com.superlogical.terminal.shell`. A `split` node divides its space in two and holds another node in each of `before` and `after`.

In a `split` node, `direction` is `horizontal` to put `before` on the left of `after`, or `vertical` to put it on top. `ratio` is the fraction of the space that `before` gets, greater than 0 and less than 1. It defaults to 0.5.
`layout` always starts new blocks. To place a detached block that already exists, use `session.move_block`.
In the new window, the first block in `block_ids` has focus.
Either the whole layout is created or none of it is. If a block fails to start, the server closes the blocks it already started, and the call fails.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `layout` is missing or malformed, or a `flavor` is malformed, it fails with `bad_request`, and if no creator provides a `flavor`, it fails with `not_found`.
If the call would go past a limit on windows per session, blocks per window, or blocks on the server, it fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: session.own_block
methods.description: Claim blocks for the calling client. The result lists each block's owner.

block_ids.description: The blocks to claim. Leave it out or empty to claim every block in the session.

mode.description: How to claim them. 'take' makes the calling client the owner right away. 'request' makes it the owner only of blocks that have none, and it may get the rest when their owner gives them up or leaves. Defaults to take.

block_id.description: The block's ID.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: Each claimed block and its owner after this call.

validation_notes: When the clients attached to a session want different things for a block, such as a terminal's size, the block follows its owner. Owning a block gives no other rights over it.
The calling client must be attached to the session, with `session.attach` or `session.bootstrap`. A connection that only called `session.attach_all` fails with `bad_request`.

Either mode puts the caller in line for the block. When the owner gives it up, detaches, or loses its connection, the block passes to the connected client in line that claimed it most recently, with any `take` ahead of every `request`.
An owner whose connection drops gets each of its blocks back when it reconnects, unless that block's owner has changed again since.
`blocks` lists each block's owner after the call, in the order of `block_ids`, with a repeated ID listed once. When you claim every block, they are sorted by `block_id`.
Every change of owner sends `block_owner_changed`. If a block in a window changes owner, the call also sends one `session_view_changed`, because `session.view` shows owners.
A `mode` other than `take` or `request` fails with `bad_request`.
If any ID in `block_ids` isn't a block in the session, the call fails with `bad_request` and changes nothing.

methods.name: session.raise_layer
methods.description: Move a floating layer to the front, or just above another floating layer.

layer_id.description: The floating layer to move forward.

relative_layer_id.description: Another floating layer in the same window to place it just above. Leave it out to move it in front of every other floating layer.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: `layer_id` must name a floating layer. Naming the window's layout, the layer of kind `tiled` in `session.view`, fails the call with `bad_request`.
If the layer is already in place, the call changes nothing. Focus and the layer's bounds never change.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `layer_id` names no layer in the session, it fails with `not_found`, and if `relative_layer_id` is the same as `layer_id`, it fails with `bad_request`.
If `relative_layer_id` names a layer of kind `tiled`, or a layer in another window, the call fails with `bad_request`. If it names no layer in the session, it fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.resize_layer
methods.description: Move or resize a floating layer.

layer_id.description: The floating layer to move or resize.

bounds.description: The layer's new position and size, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height. It must fit inside the window.

anyOf.description: A rectangle as [x, y, w, h]. x and y place its top-left corner and w and h give its size, each as a fraction of the window's width or height.

x.description: The left edge, as a fraction of the window's width.

y.description: The top edge, as a fraction of the window's height.

w.description: The width, as a fraction of the window's width.

h.description: The height, as a fraction of the window's height.

anyOf.description: The same rectangle as an object, the form that earlier clients send.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: `layer_id` must name a floating layer. Naming the window's layout, the layer of kind `tiled` in `session.view`, fails the call with `bad_request`.
`bounds` is measured from the window's top-left corner. Its width and height must be greater than 0.
Focus and the order of floating layers don't change. Setting the bounds the layer already has changes nothing.
If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `layer_id` names no layer in the session, it fails with `not_found`, and bad `bounds` fail with `bad_request`.

methods.name: session.resize_pane
methods.description: Move the border between two blocks to change their sizes.

direction.description: The kind of split between the two blocks: 'horizontal' for a border between left and right, or 'vertical' for one between top and bottom.

before_block_id.description: A block on the left of the border, or above it when direction is vertical.

after_block_id.description: A block on the right of the border, or below it when direction is vertical.

ratio.description: The fraction of the split's space that the before part gets, greater than 0 and less than 1.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: The two blocks pick the border. The server finds the innermost split in `direction` that has `before_block_id` on its left or top side and `after_block_id` on its right or bottom side. The blocks don't need to touch.
`ratio` has no default. Unlike in `session.new_split`, 0 doesn't mean an even split.
The blocks can be in any window, active or not. Focus doesn't change.
The call always raises `revision` and sends `session_view_changed`, even if the border was already where you asked.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If the two block IDs are the same, or `ratio` is out of range, it fails with `bad_request`, and if either block isn't in any window, it fails with `not_found`.
If the blocks are in different windows or layers, or no split between them matches, the call fails with `bad_request`.

methods.name: session.set_block_label
methods.description: Set a block's label.

block_id.description: The block to relabel. Required.

label.description: The new label, up to 128 characters. An empty or missing label restores a default made from the block's ID.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: `block_id` is required. Leaving it out fails with `bad_request`.
The server trims whitespace from both ends of `label`. An empty `label` restores a default made from the block's ID, such as `Block 89abcdef`, rather than the flavor name a new block starts with.
A label longer than 128 characters, or one that contains a control character, fails with `bad_request`.
Relabeling a block that is in a window sends `session_view_changed`. A detached block isn't part of the view, so relabeling it sends no event and leaves `revision` unchanged.
If `block_id` names a block that isn't in the session, the call fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.set_label
methods.description: Set the session's label.

label.description: The new label, up to 128 characters. An empty or missing label restores the label the server chose when it created the session.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: The server trims whitespace from both ends of `label`. An empty `label` restores the label the server chose when it created the session, such as `quiet-meadow`. It does so even if the session was created with a label.
A label longer than 128 characters, or one that contains a control character, fails with `bad_request`.
A new label sends `session_label_changed`, then `session_view_changed`. Setting the label the session already has changes nothing.

methods.name: session.set_window_label
methods.description: Set a window's label.

label.description: The new label, up to 128 characters. An empty or missing label restores a default made from the window's ID.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: The server trims whitespace from both ends of `label`. An empty `label` restores a default made from the window's ID, such as `Window 89abcdef`.
A label longer than 128 characters, or one that contains a control character, fails with `bad_request`.
A new label sends `window_label_changed`, then `session_view_changed`. Setting the label the window already has changes nothing.
If `window_id` names a window that isn't in the session, the call fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.swap_blocks
methods.description: Swap the places of two blocks.

block_id.description: One of the two blocks to swap.

other_block_id.description: The other block. The order of the two doesn't matter.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

validation_notes: Both blocks must be in a window. They can be in different windows or layers.
Only the two blocks move. Splits, their sizes and IDs, floating layers, and the window order stay the same.
If one of the blocks has focus in the active window, focus follows it to its new place, and that place's window becomes active.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `block_id` and `other_block_id` are the same, it fails with `bad_request`. If either block isn't in any window, including a detached block, it fails with `not_found`.

methods.name: session.view
methods.description: Get the session's windows, their layouts, and their blocks in one snapshot.

revision.description: The view's revision. It goes up by one with every change, so a larger revision is a newer view of the session.

active_window_id.description: The window the session shows. Left out when the session has no windows.

focused_block_id.description: The window's focused block, which receives typing while the window is active. Left out if the window has none.

zoomed_block_id.description: The block zoomed to fill the window, if any. Layouts keep their normal sizes, so draw this block over the whole window.

kind.description: How the layer is placed: 'tiled' for the layer that fills the window, or 'floating' for a floating layer. Draw a kind you don't know as 'floating'.

bounds.description: Where the layer sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

rect.description: Where this node sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

block_id.description: The block at this node. Set only when split isn't.

split_id.description: The split's ID. It stays the same while the split exists, so you can match splits across views.

direction.description: How the space is divided: 'horizontal' puts before on the left and after on the right, and 'vertical' puts before above after. Draw a direction you don't know as 'horizontal'.

ratio.description: The fraction of the space that before gets, between 0 and 1.

before.description: The node on the left or top.

after.description: The node on the right or bottom.

split.description: How this node divides in two. Set only when block_id isn't.

layout.description: How the layer divides its space between blocks, as a tree of splits. Null when the layer is empty.

block_id.description: The block's ID.

creator_name.description: The creator that made the block, such as com.superlogical.terminal.

flavor.description: The flavor the block was made from, such as com.superlogical.terminal.shell.

host_id.description: Identifies the machine and account the block runs as. If it equals your local server's host_id, the block sees the same files you do. Otherwise treat the block as remote.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: The blocks in the layer, in layout order. The layout field says where each one sits.

layers.description: The window's layers, from back to front. The first is the tiled layer, which holds the window's layout and fills the window.

windows.description: The session's windows, in order. Rex.app shows them as tabs in this order.

validation_notes: `revision` starts at zero for a new session and goes up by one each time the view changes. Compare revisions only within one session, and keep the view with the highest revision.

A `session_view_changed` event carries only the new revision, not the view. These events can arrive out of revision order, so call `session.view` only when an event's revision is higher than the one in the view you hold.
`window_created`, `window_closed`, `window_label_changed`, `active_window_changed`, and `session_label_changed` arrive before the `session_view_changed` event for the same change.
The view holds only blocks that are in a window. `session.list_blocks` also lists detached blocks.
The view describes structure, not content. To read what a block shows, call one of its own methods, such as `com.superlogical.terminal.format`.

methods.name: session.zoom_block
methods.description: Zoom a block to fill its window, or undo the zoom.

block_id.description: The block to zoom. It takes focus, and its window becomes active. Leave it out to use the focused block of window_id, or of the active window.

window_id.description: A window whose focused block to zoom. The active window doesn't change. Send it only when block_id is left out.

zoom.description: Set true to zoom or false to restore the layout. Leave it out to switch between the two.

block_id.description: The block this call zoomed or restored. If the request didn't name one, this is the focused block the server used.

zoomed.description: Whether the block is zoomed after this call.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows.

validation_notes: With `block_id`, the server first focuses the block and makes its window active, as `session.focus_block` does. With `window_id`, focus and the active window don't change.
Zoom changes only what is shown. The layout stays the same, and the zoom ends when focus moves to another block in the window.

If the session doesn't exist, the call fails with `session_not_found`. If `block_id` names a block that isn't in any window, or `window_id` names a window that isn't in the session, it fails with `not_found`. Sending both fails with `bad_request`.
If both `block_id` and `window_id` are left out and the session has no windows, the call fails with `conflict`.

methods.name: target.complete
methods.description: List the labels, window positions, and short IDs that start with a prefix. Use it to complete a name as someone types it.

kinds.description: What to complete: session, window, block, or client, with the same rules as in target.resolve. Completions come back in this order.

prefix.description: The text typed so far. It matches the start of labels (ignoring case), window positions, and short IDs. An empty prefix matches everything.

session_id.description: The caller's session. Without scope.session, windows and blocks are searched only in this session, and an empty session query selects it.

block_id.description: The caller's block, such as the terminal a script runs in. In target.resolve, empty block and window queries default to it and its window.

client_id.description: The caller's own client. In target.resolve, an empty client query selects it if it's among the clients searched.

context.description: Where the caller is. Only session_id is used: without scope.session, windows and blocks come from that session.

session.description: The session to search in, named by ID, label, or the end of its ID. A client search then covers only clients attached to it.

window.description: The window to search in, named by ID, label, position, or the end of its ID. Allowed only when kinds is just block.

scope.description: Limits completion to one session, or block completion to one window, as in target.resolve.

value.description: The text to offer, such as a label, a window position, or a short ID.

form.description: What value is: 'label', 'ordinal' (a window position), or 'id' (a short ID, the last six hexadecimal digits of an ID).

kind.description: What this is: session, window, block, or client. Skip a candidate whose kind you don't know.

session_id.description: The session's ID, or the ID of the session that holds the window or block. Left out for a client.

window_id.description: The window's ID, or the ID of the window that holds the block. Left out for sessions, clients, and detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block's ID. Set only for blocks.

client_id.description: The client's ID. Set only for clients.

label.description: Its label, or an empty string if it has none.

ordinal.description: A window's position in its session, counting from 1, in the order session.view lists windows. Left out for everything else.

where.description: Where it is, for showing to a person, such as 'window 2' or 'detached'. For a client, the program, such as 'Rex.app 1.6.0'. May be empty. Don't parse it.

target.description: The session, window, block, or client that value names.

completions.description: Every match, grouped by kind in the order of kinds. Empty if nothing matches or a scope doesn't resolve.

validation_notes: `kinds`, `scope`, and `context.session_id` choose what to search the same way as in `target.resolve`, and the call fails with `bad_request` in the same cases.

`prefix` matches the start of labels, ignoring case, and label completions keep the label's own case. White space around `prefix` is ignored. A control character inside it, such as a tab, fails the call with `bad_request`.
Windows also match by position, so the prefix `1` matches windows 1, 10, 11, and so on. An empty prefix matches every position.

An empty prefix, or one made only of hexadecimal digits, also matches the start of short IDs. A short ID is the last six hexadecimal digits of an ID, such as `12bef5`, and `target.resolve` accepts it as the end of an ID.
One thing can appear more than once, such as a window whose label and short ID both start with the prefix.
Completions are grouped by kind, in the order of `kinds`. Within each kind, labels come first, sorted ignoring case, then window positions in order, then short IDs in sorted order.
If `scope.session` or `scope.window` matches nothing or several things, `completions` is empty. The call doesn't fail.
Detached blocks are included unless `scope.window` is set.
To complete a client, set `kinds` to `["client"]`. Clients complete by label and short ID, and each target's `where` names the program, such as `Rex.app 1.6.0`.

methods.name: target.resolve
methods.description: Look up sessions, windows, blocks, or clients by ID, label, or position. Each query gets its own result, which says whether it matched one thing, nothing, or several.

kinds.description: What each query may name: session, window, block, or client. List each kind once, and list client only on its own.

queries.description: The names to look up. Each is a full ID, a label, a window position, the end of an ID, or an empty string for the default.

session_id.description: The caller's session. Without scope.session, windows and blocks are searched only in this session, and an empty session query selects it.

block_id.description: The caller's block, such as the terminal a script runs in. In target.resolve, empty block and window queries default to it and its window.

client_id.description: The caller's own client. In target.resolve, an empty client query selects it if it's among the clients searched.

context.description: Where the caller is, such as the terminal a script runs in. IDs in it that no longer exist are ignored.

session.description: The session to search in, named by ID, label, or the end of its ID. A client search then covers only clients attached to it.

window.description: The window to search in, named by ID, label, position, or the end of its ID. Allowed only when kinds is just block.

scope.description: Limits the search to one session, or a block search to one window. Not allowed when kinds includes session.

query.description: The query this result answers, exactly as sent.

status.description: Whether the query matched: 'resolved' for one thing, 'not_found' for nothing, or 'ambiguous' for several. Treat a value you don't know as 'not_found'.

kind.description: What this is: session, window, block, or client. Skip a candidate whose kind you don't know.

session_id.description: The session's ID, or the ID of the session that holds the window or block. Left out for a client.

window_id.description: The window's ID, or the ID of the window that holds the block. Left out for sessions, clients, and detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block's ID. Set only for blocks.

client_id.description: The client's ID. Set only for clients.

label.description: Its label, or an empty string if it has none.

ordinal.description: A window's position in its session, counting from 1, in the order session.view lists windows. Left out for everything else.

where.description: Where it is, for showing to a person, such as 'window 2' or 'detached'. For a client, the program, such as 'Rex.app 1.6.0'. May be empty. Don't parse it.

target.description: What the query matched. Set only when status is resolved.

reason.description: Why the query didn't resolve, for showing to a person. May be empty.

kind.description: What this is: session, window, block, or client. Skip a candidate whose kind you don't know.

session_id.description: The session's ID, or the ID of the session that holds the window or block. Left out for a client.

window_id.description: The window's ID, or the ID of the window that holds the block. Left out for sessions, clients, and detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block's ID. Set only for blocks.

client_id.description: The client's ID. Set only for clients.

label.description: Its label, or an empty string if it has none.

ordinal.description: A window's position in its session, counting from 1, in the order session.view lists windows. Left out for everything else.

where.description: Where it is, for showing to a person, such as 'window 2' or 'detached'. For a client, the program, such as 'Rex.app 1.6.0'. May be empty. Don't parse it.

candidates.description: When status is ambiguous, the choices for a person to pick from. Check each one's kind.

results.description: One result for each query, in the same order as queries.

validation_notes: List at least one kind in `kinds`, each only once, and `client` only on its own, or the call fails with `bad_request`. A kind the server doesn't know fails the same way, which can happen when the server is older than your client.

Send at least one query, or the call fails with `bad_request`. Each query gets one entry in `results`, in the same order. A query that matches nothing or several things doesn't fail the call: its `status` is `not_found` or `ambiguous`.

The server tries each query in four steps and stops at the first step that matches anything: full ID, label (ignoring case), window position, then the end of an ID (4 to 32 hexadecimal digits). So a window labeled `2` wins over the second window. If the winning step matches more than one thing, the result is `ambiguous`.
A query that starts like a full ID, such as `block:`, is only tried as a full ID. Its result is `not_found` if the ID is malformed, if `kinds` doesn't include that kind, or if nothing has that ID.
Only windows have positions. `1` is the first window in its session, in the order Rex.app shows them as tabs. When several sessions are searched, a position can match a window in each one.

When `kinds` lists more than one kind, one query can match different kinds of things, such as a session and a window with the same label. The result is then `ambiguous`, and each candidate's `kind` says what it is.

Without `scope.session`, windows and blocks are searched only in the session named by `context.session_id`. If that's left out or the session no longer exists, every session is searched. This applies to full IDs too, so the full ID of a block in another session is `not_found`.

If a scope matches nothing or several things, every result gets that `not_found` or `ambiguous` status, and its `reason` says which scope failed. For an ambiguous scope, `candidates` lists what the scope could mean.

An empty query, or one of only spaces, asks for a default, such as the block a script runs in. When `kinds` lists several kinds, an empty query gets the default for the most specific one: block, then window, then session.
An empty session query selects `context.session_id`, or the only session if there's just one. With no sessions it's `not_found`, and with several it's `ambiguous`.

An empty window query selects the window that holds `context.block_id`, or else the active window of the session being searched. If several sessions are searched, it's `ambiguous` even with `context.block_id` set, and `candidates` lists the sessions to choose from.

An empty block query selects `context.block_id` if that block is among those searched. Otherwise it selects the focused block of the window an empty window query would choose. With `scope.window`, it ignores `context.block_id` and selects that window's focused block.

Block searches include detached blocks, which are running but aren't placed in any window. `scope.window` leaves them out. A block's `where` reads `window 2` or `detached`. When several sessions are searched, it names the session too, as in `window 2 of work`, and a window's `where` reads `in work`.

To look up a connected client, such as Rex.app, set `kinds` to `["client"]`. A client query matches a full ID, a label, or the end of an ID, since clients have no positions. Every connected client is searched, unless `scope.session` limits the search to clients attached to that session.

An empty client query selects `context.client_id` if that client is among those searched. Otherwise it selects the only client that reported its kind as `app` when it connected, such as Rex.app. With no app it's `not_found`, and with several it's `ambiguous`.

`scope.window` is looked up among the sessions being searched. The call fails with `bad_request` if `kinds` includes `session` and `scope` is sent, even as an empty object, or if `scope.window` is set and `kinds` isn't just `block`. A query or scope that contains a control character, such as a newline, fails the same way.

methods.name: blob_read
methods.description: Read a result that was too large for one reply or event, such as the output of format with max_bytes set, or a selection_copied event without text. The server keeps each result for about five minutes.

id.description: The result to read, from the reply or event that named it, such as the id in a format reply or a selection_copied event. Zero or left out reads the newest result, whatever produced it. If the server no longer has the result, the call fails with not_found.

offset.description: Where to start reading, in bytes from the start of the result. To read the next part, add the length in bytes of the data you received. Must not be negative.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of data to return, measured once it is encoded as a JSON string. Zero or left out means 49152 (48 KiB), and values above 983040 (960 KiB) are lowered to that. Must not be negative.

id.description: The result that was read. Send it in later requests so that every part comes from the same result.

data.description: The text read, starting at offset. It never ends partway through a character. It can be shorter than max_bytes even when more text remains.

total.description: The length of the whole result, in bytes.

eof.description: True if data reaches the end of the result.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of data to return, measured once it is encoded as a JSON string. Zero or left out means 49152 (48 KiB), and values above 983040 (960 KiB) are lowered to that. Must not be negative.

id.description: The copy that was read. Send it in later requests so that every part comes from the same copy.

data.description: The text read, starting at offset. It never ends partway through a character. It can be shorter than max_bytes even when more text remains.

total.description: The length of the whole copied text, in bytes.

id.description: The record's ID. A slash separates a parent from a child, as in build/test. Left out for the root record, which holds the reports that give no ID.

state.description: What the program says it is doing: 'idle', 'working', 'done', 'blocked' (waiting for the user), or 'error'. Treat a value you don't know as 'idle'.

kind.description: What a blocked program is waiting for: 'permission', 'question', or 'auth' (a password or other credential). Left out if the program didn't say. Treat a value you don't know as if it were left out.

progress.description: How far along the program is, as a percentage from 0 to 100. Only working and blocked records have one, and only if the program reported it.

app.description: The program's name, such as cargo or terraform, exactly as it reported it.

effective_app.description: The name of the program the record belongs to: app if it is set, or else the app of the nearest parent record that has one. Left out if no record in the chain has an app.

title.description: A short label for the record, such as the name of a task. It comes from the program, so show it as plain text.

msg.description: One line of text describing the status. Show it as plain text. A client may shorten it but shouldn't try to interpret it.

updated_at.description: When the report arrived, by the server's clock, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

name.description: The process's name, found the same way as name in the result of process. Compare it as well as pid, because the system reuses process IDs.

owner.description: The terminal's foreground process when the report arrived. Left out if the server couldn't tell.

records.description: Every record, sorted by id. The root record comes first, and each parent comes before its children. Empty if no program has reported a status.

validation_notes: Call it as `com.superlogical.terminal.program_status` with `session_id`, `block_id`, and this method's own arguments under `args`.

methods.name: pwd
methods.description: Get the working directory that a program in the terminal last reported. To find where each process actually is, call process instead.

pwd.description: The reported directory: a file:// URL when the program used OSC 7, or a plain path otherwise. Left out if no directory has been reported or a reset cleared it.

name.description: The process's name, found the same way as name in the result of process. Compare it as well as pid, because the system reuses process IDs.

owner.description: The process that reported the directory. Left out if pwd is left out or the server couldn't tell.

validation_notes: Call it as `com.superlogical.terminal.pwd` with `session_id`, `block_id`, and this method's own arguments under `args`.

methods.name: reset
methods.description: Reset the terminal to its starting state and clear the screen and scrollback. The program keeps running, and the size and default colors stay the same.

actions.name: reset
actions.title: Reset Terminal
actions.description: Return the terminal to its starting state and clear the screen and scrollback.

methods.name: resize
methods.description: Request a terminal size in columns and rows. It applies at once if the caller owns the block or no client does, and otherwise when the caller becomes the owner.

columns.description: The width in columns, that is, characters per line, from 1 to 65535.

rows.description: The height in rows, from 1 to 65535.

cell_width_px.description: The width of one character cell in pixels, from 1 to 65535. Send it together with cell_height_px, or leave both out to keep the current cell size.

cell_height_px.description: The height of one character cell in pixels, from 1 to 65535. Send it together with cell_width_px, or leave both out to keep the current cell size.

validation_notes: Call it as `com.superlogical.terminal.resize` with `session_id`, `block_id`, and this method's own arguments under `args`.

methods.name: set_theme
methods.description: Replace the terminal's default colors. As with resize, they apply at once if the caller owns the block or no client does, and otherwise when the caller becomes the owner.

foreground.description: The default text color, as hex RRGGBB or #RRGGBB, such as #d6deeb. Empty or left out uses the built-in color.

background.description: The default background color, as hex RRGGBB or #RRGGBB, such as #011627. Empty or left out uses the built-in color.

cursor.description: The cursor color, as hex RRGGBB or #RRGGBB, such as #80a4c2. Empty or left out uses the built-in color.

palette.description: Changes to the 256-color palette, each written as index=RRGGBB or index=#RRGGBB with an index from 0 to 255, such as 1=#ef5350. Colors not listed keep their built-in values.

scheme.description: Whether the theme is 'light' or 'dark', which programs in the terminal can ask for. If empty, the terminal decides from how bright background is, and treats no background as dark.

validation_notes: Call it as `com.superlogical.terminal.set_theme` with `session_id`, `block_id`, and this method's own arguments under `args`.

methods.name: size
methods.description: Get the terminal's size, its owner, and the size each client last requested.

cell_width_px.description: The width of one character cell in pixels.

cell_height_px.description: The height of one character cell in pixels.

owner.description: The client that owns the block, whose size the terminal uses. Null if the block has no owner.

client_id.description: The client that requested this size.

updated_at.description: When the server received the request, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

desired.description: The last size each client requested, the owner's included, newest first.

methods.name: title
methods.description: Get the terminal's title and the process that set it.

title.description: The terminal's title, as a program last set it. Empty if no title is set.

name.description: The process's name, found the same way as name in the result of process. Compare it as well as pid, because the system reuses process IDs.

owner.description: The process that set the title, as title_changed reported it. Left out if no title is set, a reset cleared it, or the server couldn't tell.

methods.name: write
methods.description: Type text into the terminal as if the user had typed it. The call returns once the text is queued, without waiting for the program to read it.

data.description: The text to type. It can hold escape sequences for keys that aren't text, such as \u001b[A for the up arrow.

bytes_written.description: The number of bytes queued, which is the length of data in UTF-8 bytes, not characters.

validation_notes: Call it as `com.superlogical.terminal.write` with `session_id`, `block_id`, and this method's own arguments under `args`.
